newsitem.title: FRANCE: France rules out staying in Bosnia if U.S. leaves.
newsitem.headline: France rules out staying in Bosnia if U.S. leaves.

text.p: France on Sunday ruled out keeping troops in Bosnia on a NATO-led peace mission next year if the United States pulls its forces out.
"There is no question of our acting alone as some people have suggested," Defence Minister Charles Millon told Europe 1 radio.

"Our position has never varied. We came in the framework of IFOR (Implementation Force) and we will stay in the framework of IFOR with the United States. But we will leave Bosnia if the United States leaves Bosnia," he said.

The mandate for the 58,000-strong IFOR mission, sent to Bosnia to oversee the implementation of the Dayton peace accords after the 3-1/2-year war, runs out in December. NATO countries are edging towards a new commitment.
IFOR includes other NATO members, such as Britain, and 18 non-NATO countries, among them Russia and Ukraine.
"We'll all stay together or we will all leave together. And if we leave, we will have to think about ways and means of guaranteeing peace in Bosnia," Millon said.
He hailed planning for a joint Franco-German peacekeeping force in Bosnia once the current mandate runs out as an important sign of increasing European defence cooperation.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said last week the two nations had made advanced preparations for a joint peacekeeping force, the first such direct use of German troops in a potential combat role outside the NATO area since World War Two.
